sentences.zh: 丙午，次河池郡，崔圓奏劍南歲稔民安，儲供無闕，上大悅，授圓中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，蜀郡長史、劍南節度如故。

translations.literal: On bingwu they halted at Hechi commandery; Cui Yuan memorialized that in Sword South the year's harvest was good and the people at peace, with abundant stores—the emperor was greatly pleased and made Yuan Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor, retaining his posts as chief of Shu and Sword South commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At Hechi Cui Yuan reported Shu was stocked with grain; the emperor made him vice director and councillor.

sentences.zh: 以前華州刺史魏犀為梁州長史。

translations.literal: Former Huazhou prefect Wei Xi was made chief of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xi became Liangzhou chief.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸丑朔。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month on guichou, the first day of the month.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh month opened on guichou.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，次益昌縣，渡吉柏江，有雙魚夾舟而躍，議者以為龍。

translations.literal: On renxu they halted at Yichang county, crossed the Jibai River, and a pair of fish leaped on either side of the boat; debaters took it for a dragon.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu at Yichang twin fish leaped beside the boat—omen of a dragon, men said.

sentences.zh: 甲子，次普安郡，憲部侍郎房琯自後至，上與語甚悅，即日拜為吏部尚書、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: On jiazi they halted at Pu'an commandery; Vice Minister of Justice Fang Guan arrived from behind; the emperor spoke with him at great length and that same day made him Minister of Personnel and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi at Pu'an Fang Guan caught up and was made personnel minister and councillor the same day.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，詔以皇太子諱充天下兵馬元帥，都統朔方、河東、河北、平盧等節度兵馬，收復兩京；

translations.literal: On dingmao an edict made the crown prince supreme commander of all armies, commanding the military commissioners of Shuofang, Hedong, Hebei, Pinglu, and the rest to recover the two capitals;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the crown prince was made supreme commander to retake the two capitals;

sentences.zh: 永王璘江陵府都督，統山南東路、黔中、江南西路等節度大使；

translations.literal: Prince Yong Wang Lin Governor of Jiangling, supreme commander of Shannan East Circuit, Qianzhong, Jiangnan West Circuit, and other commissioners;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong Lin governed Jiangling over the southern circuits;

sentences.zh: 盛王琦廣陵郡大都督，統江南東路、淮南、河南等路節度大使；

translations.literal: Prince Sheng Wang Qi Grand Governor of Guangling, supreme commander of Jiangnan East Circuit, Huainan, Henan, and other routes;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sheng Qi held Huainan and the lower Yangzi;

sentences.zh: 豐王珙武威郡都督，領河西、隴石、安西、北庭等路節度大使。

translations.literal: Prince Feng Wang Gong Governor of Wuwei, commanding Hexi, Longyou, Anxi, Beiting, and other routes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Feng Gong held the northwest frontiers.

sentences.zh: 初，京師陷賊，車駕倉皇出幸，人未知所向，眾心震駭，及聞是詔，遠近相慶，咸思效忠於興復。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the capital fell to the rebels, the imperial carriage had fled in haste and none knew whither; hearts were shaken. When this edict was heard, far and near rejoiced and all wished to devote loyalty to restoration.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell none knew where the emperor fled; this edict made the realm hope again for restoration.

sentences.zh: 庚午，次巴西郡，太守崔渙奉迎。

translations.literal: On gengwu they halted at Baxi commandery; prefect Cui Huan came out to welcome.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu at Baxi Cui Huan welcomed the court.

sentences.zh: 即日以渙為門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: That same day Huan was made Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: That day Cui Huan became vice chancellor.

sentences.zh: 以韋見素為左相。

translations.literal: Wei Jiansu was made Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiansu became left chancellor.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，車駕至蜀郡，扈從官吏軍士到者一千三百人，宮女二十四人而已。

translations.literal: On gengchen the imperial carriage reached Shu commandery; of attending officials, soldiers, and servitors who arrived there were only one thousand three hundred, and palace women only twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the court reached Chengdu—thirteen hundred followers and twenty-four palace women.

sentences.zh: 八月癸未朔，禦蜀都府衙，宣詔曰：「朕以薄德，嗣守神器，每乾乾惕厲，勤念生靈，一物失所，無忘罪己。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the first day of the eighth month, he held court at the yamen of the Shu capital and proclaimed an edict, saying, “I, of slight virtue, have succeeded in guarding the sacred vessel. Constantly I am diligent and wary, mindful of the living; if one thing is lost, I do not forget to blame myself.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei he held court at Chengdu and began an edict confessing slight virtue and constant care for the people.

sentences.zh: 聿來四紀，人亦小康，推心於人，不疑於物。

translations.literal: For nearly four reign-periods the people have known modest peace; I have given my heart to others and not doubted things.
translations.idiomatic: For four reign-periods the people had known modest peace; he had trusted others without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 而奸臣兇豎，棄義背恩，割剝黎元，擾亂區夏，皆朕不明之過也。

translations.literal: Yet treacherous ministers and vicious underlings abandoned righteousness and betrayed grace, flaying the black-haired people and disturbing the realm—all my own want of clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Traitors had flayed the people and disturbed the realm—all his own want of clarity.

sentences.zh: 今巡撫巴蜀，訓厲師徒，仍令太子諸王蒐兵重鎮，誅夷兇醜，以謝昊穹；

translations.literal: Now I tour and instruct Ba and Shu, train armies and soldiers, and still order the crown prince and imperial princes to gather troops at strategic posts, execute the vicious and foul, to answer Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: He would train armies in Ba-Shu, order princes to gather troops, and execute the vicious to answer Heaven;

sentences.zh: 思與群臣重弘理道，可大赦天下。

translations.literal: I desire with the ministers again to enlarge the Way of governance—a great amnesty for all under Heaven.”
translations.idiomatic: and with his ministers enlarge the Way of governance—a great amnesty for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」癸巳，靈武使至，始知皇太子即位。

translations.literal: On guisi an envoy from Lingwu arrived; they first learned that the crown prince had ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi word came from Lingwu that the crown prince had become emperor.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，上用靈武冊稱上皇，詔稱誥。

translations.literal: On dingyou the emperor used the Lingwu investiture and styled himself Retired Emperor; edicts were styled pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou he took the title Retired Emperor and styled his orders pronouncements.

sentences.zh: 己亥，上皇臨軒冊肅宗，命宰臣韋見素、房琯使靈武，冊命曰：「朕稱太上皇，軍國大事先取皇帝處分，後奏朕知。

translations.literal: On jihai the Retired Emperor faced the hall to invest Su Zong; he ordered chancellors Wei Jiansu and Fang Guan to go to Lingwu. The investiture order read: “I style myself Retired Emperor; military and state affairs are first decided by the emperor and afterward reported to my knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he invested Suzong at court and sent Jiansu and Fang Guan to Lingwu: military affairs would pass through the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 候克復兩京，朕當怡神姑射，偃息大庭。

translations.literal: When the two capitals are recovered, I shall nourish my spirit at Guye and rest in the great court.”
translations.idiomatic: When the capitals were recovered he would retire to nourish his spirit and rest from rule.
The investiture edict closed there.

sentences.zh: 明年九月，郭子儀收復兩京。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the following year Guo Ziyi recovered the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: The next ninth month Guo Ziyi retook the two capitals.

sentences.zh: 十月，肅宗遣中使啖廷瑤入蜀奉迎。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Suzong sent Palace Attendant Dan Tingyao into Shu to escort him back.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Suzong sent Dan Tingyao to bring him home from Shu.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，上皇發蜀郡。

translations.literal: On dingmao the Retired Emperor departed Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he left Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙申，次鳳翔郡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on bingchen he halted at Fengxiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he reached Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 肅宗遣精騎三千至扶風迎衛。

translations.literal: Suzong sent three thousand elite horsemen to Fufeng to escort and guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong sent three thousand cavalry to meet him at Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙午，肅宗具法駕至咸陽望賢驛迎奉。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the twelfth month, Suzong came in full imperial regalia to Wangxian post station in Xianyang to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Suzong met him at Wangxian post in full regalia.

sentences.zh: 上皇御宮之南樓，肅宗拜慶樓下，嗚咽流涕不自勝，為上皇徒步控轡，上皇撫背止之，即騎馬前導。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor mounted the south tower of the palace; Suzong bowed below the Tower of Celebration, weeping uncontrollably. He walked before the Retired Emperor holding the reins; the Retired Emperor stroked his back to stop him, then rode ahead as guide.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son met at Wangxian: Suzong wept, tried to lead the horse, and the retired emperor gently refused.

sentences.zh: 丁未，至京師，文武百僚、京城士庶夾道歡呼，靡不流涕。

translations.literal: On dingwei they reached the capital; civil and military officials and the people of the capital lined the roads shouting for joy, none without tears.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Chang'an lined the roads in tears of joy.

sentences.zh: 即日御大明宮之含元殿，見百僚，上皇親自撫問。

translations.literal: That day he held court in the Hall of Encompassing Primordium of the Great Bright Palace and saw the hundred officials; the Retired Emperor personally comforted and inquired of each.
translations.idiomatic: That day he sat in the Hall of Encompassing Primordium and spoke to each minister.

sentences.zh: 人人感咽。

translations.literal: Every man was moved to weeping.
translations.idiomatic: All wept.

sentences.zh: 時太廟為賊所焚，權移神主於大內長安殿，上皇謁廟請罪，遂幸興慶宮。

translations.literal: At the time the Imperial Ancestral Temple had been burned by the rebels; the spirit tablets were temporarily moved to the Chang'an Hall of the inner palace. The Retired Emperor worshipped at the temple to confess guilt, then went to Xingqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple was burned; he worshipped the moved tablets and went to Xingqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 三載二月，肅宗與群臣奉上皇尊號曰太上至道聖皇帝。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year Suzong and the ministers presented the Retired Emperor the honorific Retired Emperor of the Supreme Way and Sagely Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Suzong gave him the title Retired Emperor of the Supreme Way and Sagely Sovereign.

sentences.zh: 乾元三年七月丁未，移幸西內之甘露殿。

translations.literal: On dingwei of the seventh month of Qianyuan 3 he moved to the Sweet Dew Hall in the Western Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On Qianyuan 3, seventh month, he moved to Sweet Dew Hall in the western palace.

sentences.zh: 時閹宦李輔國離間肅宗，故移居西內。

translations.literal: At the time the eunuch Li Fuguo drove a wedge between father and son; hence the move to the western inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Li Fuguo had estranged father and son, so he was moved west.

sentences.zh: 高力士、陳玄禮等遷謫，上皇浸不自懌。

translations.literal: Gao Lishi, Chen Xuanli, and others were banished; the Retired Emperor grew ever less at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi and Chen Xuanli were exiled; the retired emperor sank into gloom.

sentences.zh: 上元二年四月甲寅，崩於神龍殿，時年七十八。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Shangyuan 2, on jiayin, he died in the Hall of Divine Dragon at the age of seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin of Shangyuan 2 he died in the Hall of Divine Dragon, aged seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 群臣上謚曰至道大聖大明孝皇帝，廟號玄宗。

translations.literal: The ministers gave the posthumous title Retired Emperor of the Supreme Way, Great Sagely, Great Bright Filial Emperor; his temple name was Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously styled Retired Emperor of the Supreme Way, Great Sagely, Great Bright Filial Emperor, temple name Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 初，上皇親拜五陵，至橋陵，見金粟山崗有龍盤鳳翥之勢，復近先塋，謂侍臣曰：「吾千秋後宜葬此地，得奉先陵，不忘孝敬矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Retired Emperor in person worshipped at the five tombs and reached Qiao Tomb, he saw on the golden millet hillock the momentum of a dragon coiling and a phoenix soaring, again near the former burial mound. He said to his attendants, “After my thousand autumns I should be buried in this place, able to attend the former tombs— not forgetting filial respect.”
translations.idiomatic: At Qiao tomb he chose his own grave on a dragon-and-phoenix hillock beside his forebears.

sentences.zh: 」至是，追奉先旨以創寢園，以廣德元年三月辛酉葬於泰陵。

translations.literal: At this time they followed his former command to establish the burial park and on xinyou of the third month of Guangde 1 buried him at Tai Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Tai Tomb on Guangde 1, third month, xinyou, as he had wished.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：孔子稱「王者必世而後仁」。

translations.literal: [Appraisal] The historian says: Confucius said, “A king must pass through generations before benevolence is achieved.”
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Confucius held that true kingship needs generations to ripen into benevolence.

sentences.zh: 李氏自武後移國三十餘年，朝廷罕有正人，附麗無非險輩。

translations.literal: For more than thirty years after the Li clan, when Empress Wu shifted the state, the court rarely had upright men; those who attached themselves were none but the dangerous.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years after Wu Zetian seized power the court had few honest men and many who clung to the vicious.

sentences.zh: 持苞苴而請謁，奔走權門；

translations.literal: Holding bribes they begged audience and ran to the gates of power;
translations.idiomatic: They bought office with gifts and ran to powerful gates;

sentences.zh: 效鷹犬以飛馳，中傷端士。

translations.literal: like hawks and dogs they flew to slander upright gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: like hawks and hounds they flew to ruin the upright.

sentences.zh: 以致斷喪王室，屠害宗枝。

translations.literal: Thus they severed and ruined the royal house and slaughtered the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: So the royal house was broken and the imperial clan slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 骨鯁大臣，屢遭誣陷，舞文酷吏，坐致顯榮。

translations.literal: Stalwart great ministers were repeatedly framed; cruel clerks who twisted the law sat in glory.
translations.idiomatic: Bone-hard ministers were framed again and again while legalist butchers won glory.

sentences.zh: 禮儀無復興行，刑政壞於犬馬，端揆出阿黨之語，冕旒有和事之名，朋比成風，廉恥都盡。

translations.literal: Rites and music no longer flourished; punishments and government were ruined worse than by dogs and horses. The chief ministers uttered the language of flatterers; the imperial cap bore the name of one who harmonized affairs—faction became the wind, and shame was utterly gone.
translations.idiomatic: Rites died, justice became a kennel, ministers flattered, and faction drowned shame.

sentences.zh: 我開元之有天下也，糾之以典刑，明之以禮樂，愛之以慈儉，律之以軌儀。

translations.literal: When we of Kaiyuan possessed the realm we corrected it with statutes, clarified it with rites and music, cherished it with kindness and thrift, and measured it with standards.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan we corrected the realm with law, clarified it with ritual, tempered it with kindness and thrift, and bound it with measure.

sentences.zh: 黜前朝徼幸之臣，杜其奸也；

translations.literal: We dismissed the fortune-seeking ministers of the previous court and blocked their treachery;
translations.idiomatic: We dismissed the previous court's fortune-hunters and blocked treachery;

sentences.zh: 焚後庭珠翠之玩，戒其奢也；

translations.literal: we burned the pearl and jade playthings of the rear palaces and warned against extravagance;
translations.idiomatic: we burned the rear palace's pearls and jades and warned against extravagance;

sentences.zh: 禁女樂而出宮嬪，明其教也；

translations.literal: we forbade women's music and sent palace women out, making the teaching clear;
translations.idiomatic: we banned women's music, sent palace women out, and made teaching clear;

sentences.zh: 賜酺賞而放哇淫，懼其荒也；

translations.literal: we granted feasts and rewards and released vulgar music, fearing dissipation;
translations.idiomatic: we feasted the realm yet banished vulgar song, fearing dissipation;

sentences.zh: 敘友于而敦骨肉，厚其俗也；

translations.literal: we ordered brotherly affection and thickened kinship, enriching the custom;
translations.idiomatic: we honored brotherhood and thickened kin ties;

sentences.zh: 蒐兵而責帥，明軍法也；

translations.literal: we gathered troops and held commanders accountable, making military law clear;
translations.idiomatic: we mustered troops and held generals accountable;

sentences.zh: 朝集而計最，校吏能也。

translations.literal: we held court assemblies and reckoned merit, comparing officials' ability.
translations.idiomatic: we assembled the court and ranked officials by merit.

sentences.zh: 廟堂之上，無非經濟之才；

translations.literal: In the hall there were none who were not men of statecraft;
translations.idiomatic: In the hall none lacked statecraft;

sentences.zh: 表著之中，皆得論思之士。

translations.literal: among the memorials all were men fit for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: among memorials all were fit for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 而又旁求宏碩，講道藝文。

translations.literal: Moreover we sought broadly for great scholars and lectured on the arts and letters.
translations.idiomatic: We sought great scholars and lectured on the classics.

sentences.zh: 昌言嘉謨，日聞於獻納；

translations.literal: Good words and excellent plans were daily heard in remonstrance and submission;
translations.idiomatic: Good counsel came daily at the throne;

sentences.zh: 長轡遠馭，志在於升平。

translations.literal: holding long reins and driving far, the will was set on ascending to peace.
translations.idiomatic: With long reins and a distant view we aimed at peace.

sentences.zh: 貞觀之風，一朝復振。

translations.literal: The style of Zhenguan was in one morning restored.
translations.idiomatic: In a morning the Zhenguan age seemed reborn.

sentences.zh: 於斯時也，烽燧不驚，華戎同軌。

translations.literal: In that time beacon fires were not alarmed; Chinese and barbarian shared the same track.
translations.idiomatic: Then the frontier was quiet and barbarian and Chinese shared one road.

sentences.zh: 西蕃君長，越繩橋而競款玉關；

translations.literal: Western barbarian chieftains crossed the rope bridge and vied to offer tribute at Jade Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Western chiefs crossed rope bridges to offer tribute at Jade Gate;

sentences.zh: 北狄酋渠，捐毳幕而爭趨雁塞。

translations.literal: northern Di chieftains cast aside felt tents and strove to hurry to Wild Goose Pass.
translations.idiomatic: northern chiefs threw down their tents and raced to Wild Goose Pass.

sentences.zh: 象郡、炎州之玩，雞林、鯷海之珍，莫不結轍於象胥，駢羅於典屬。

translations.literal: Curios of Elephant commandery and Hot Prefecture, treasures of Silla and the herring sea—all without exception came in caravans through the interpreters and crowded the offices of protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Exotic goods from the far south and far east crowded the interpreters' road to the capital.

sentences.zh: 膜拜丹墀之下，夷歌立仗之前，可謂冠帶百蠻，車書萬里。

translations.literal: Kowtowing below the cinnabar steps, barbarian songs before the guard of honor—one may say the hundred barbarians wore caps and belts and carts and writing reached ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: They kowtowed on the cinnabar steps and sang barbarian airs before the guard—caps and belts on every frontier, carts and writing for ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 天子乃覽雲臺之義，草泥金之札，然後封日觀，禪云亭，訪道於穆清，怡神於玄牝，與民休息，比屋可封。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven then reviewed the meaning of the Cloud Terrace, drafted the clay-and-gold letter, and afterward enfeoffed Riguanshan and performed the Border sacrifice at Yunting; sought the Way in the clear heavens, rested his spirit in the dark female; let the people rest; every house could be sealed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read Cloud Terrace precedent, drafted the clay-and-gold missive, then enfeoffed Riguanshan and sacrificed at Yunting, sought the Way in clear heaven, rested spirit in the dark female, let the people breathe, and made every household fit to seal.

sentences.zh: 於時垂髫之倪，皆知禮讓；

translations.literal: At that time children with hair in tufts all knew courtesy and yielding;
translations.idiomatic: Children in topknots all knew courtesy;

sentences.zh: 戴白之老，不識兵戈。

translations.literal: elders with white hair did not know weapons of war.
translations.idiomatic: white-haired elders had never seen arms.

sentences.zh: 虜不敢乘月犯邊，士不敢彎弓報怨。

translations.literal: Barbarians dared not raid the borders by moonlight; soldiers dared not bend the bow to avenge grievances.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians would not raid by moonlight; soldiers would not bend the bow for private revenge.

sentences.zh: 「康哉」之頌，溢於八紘。

translations.literal: The ode “How peaceful!” overflowed the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: The “How peaceful!” ode flooded the eight directions.

sentences.zh: 所謂「世而後仁」，見於開元者矣。

translations.literal: What is called “benevolence after a generation” was seen in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: The “benevolence after a generation” of the saying appeared in Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 年逾三紀，可謂太平。

translations.literal: More than three decades had passed—this may be called great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty years and more—this was great peace.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Woe!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 國無賢臣，聖亦難理；

translations.literal: Without worthy ministers, even a sage finds rule hard;
translations.idiomatic: Without worthy ministers, even a sage cannot govern;

sentences.zh: 山有猛虎，獸不敢窺。

translations.literal: when a mountain holds a fierce tiger, beasts dare not peer in.
translations.idiomatic: where a mountain holds a tiger, beasts dare not look in.

sentences.zh: 得人者昌，信不虛語。

translations.literal: He who gains men flourishes—truly no empty saying.
translations.idiomatic: Gain the right men and the state thrives—the saying is true.

sentences.zh: 昔齊桓公行同禽獸，不失霸主之名；

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Huan of Qi behaved like the beasts yet did not lose the name of hegemon;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi lived like a beast yet kept the hegemon’s name;

sentences.zh: 梁武帝靜比桑門，竟被臺城之酷。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang was quiet as a monk yet in the end suffered the cruelty of Taicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wudi was still as a monk yet died in Taicheng’s torment.

sentences.zh: 蓋得管仲則淫不害霸，任硃異則善不救亡。

translations.literal: Having Guan Zhong, debauchery did not harm the hegemony; employing Zhu Yi, virtue could not save from ruin.
translations.idiomatic: With Guan Zhong, license did not break the hegemony; with Zhu Yi, virtue could not save the throne.

sentences.zh: 開元之初，賢臣當國，四門俱穆，百度唯貞，而釋、老之流，頗以無為請見。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan worthy ministers held the state; all four gates were solemn and every measure upright, yet Daoist and Buddhist circles often asked audience pleading nonaction.
translations.idiomatic: Early Kaiyuan had worthy ministers at court, every gate solemn and every measure straight—yet Daoists and Buddhists often begged audience for nonaction.

sentences.zh: 上乃務清凈，事薰修，留連軒後之文，舞詠伯陽之說，雖稍移於勤倦，亦未至於怠荒。

translations.literal: The emperor then pursued purity, devoted himself to incense and cultivation, lingered over compositions from behind the hall, danced and chanted Laozi’s teaching—though he shifted somewhat from diligence to weariness, he had not yet reached neglect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to purity and ritual cultivation, lingered over hall compositions, danced to Laozi’s words—weariness grew, but not yet neglect.

sentences.zh: 俄而朝野怨咨，政刑紕繆，何哉？

translations.literal: Soon court and countryside groaned; government and punishments tangled—why?
translations.idiomatic: Soon court and countryside groaned; law and punishment snarled—why?

sentences.zh: 用人之失也。

translations.literal: Failure in the use of men.
translations.idiomatic: Failure in appointing men.

sentences.zh: 自天寶已還，小人道長。

translations.literal: From Tianbao onward the way of petty men grew long.
translations.idiomatic: From Tianbao on, petty men’s way lengthened.

sentences.zh: 如山有朽壞，雖大必虧；

translations.literal: As when a mountain has inner rot, though great it must crumble;
translations.idiomatic: As a mountain rots within, though great it must fall;

sentences.zh: 木有蠹蟲，其榮易落。

translations.literal: when a tree has bore-worms, its glory is easily shed.
translations.idiomatic: when a tree has bore-worms, its crown soon drops.

sentences.zh: 以百口百心之讒諂，蔽兩目兩耳之聰明，茍非鐵腸石心，安得不惑！

translations.literal: With a hundred mouths and hearts of slander screening the two eyes and two ears of intelligence, unless one had an iron gut and stone heart, how could one not be deluded!
translations.idiomatic: A hundred slandering mouths and hearts blinded two eyes and two ears—without iron bowels and a stone heart, who would not be lost?

sentences.zh: 而獻可替否，靡聞姚、宋之言；

translations.literal: Yet offerable criticism and rejection of error—none heard the words of Yao Chong and Song Jing;
translations.idiomatic: Offerable criticism went unheard from Yao and Song;

sentences.zh: 妒賢害功，但有甫、忠之奏。

translations.literal: jealous of worthies and harming merit—there were only memorials from Li and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: jealous slander of worthies heard only Li and Yang.

sentences.zh: 豪猾因茲而睥睨，明哲於是乎卷懷，故祿山之徒，得行其偽。

translations.literal: The crafty thereby leered; the clear-minded thereupon folded their plans—so An Lushan’s kind could enact their deceit.
translations.idiomatic: The crafty leered; the wise folded their plans—so An Lushan’s kind could play their fraud.

sentences.zh: 厲階之作，匪降自天，謀之不臧，前功並棄。

translations.literal: The source of calamity did not descend from Heaven; poor counsel cast prior achievements aside.
translations.idiomatic: The calamity’s source did not fall from heaven—bad counsel threw away prior merit.

sentences.zh: 惜哉！

translations.literal: A pity!
translations.idiomatic: Pity!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：開元握圖，永鑒前車。

translations.literal: 【Eulogy】 The eulogy says: Kaiyuan grasped the chart and forever took the overturned cart as mirror.
translations.idiomatic: 【Eulogy】 The eulogy says: Kaiyuan held the chart and forever mirrored the overturned cart.

sentences.zh: 景氣融朗，昏氛滌除。

translations.literal: Prosperous aura blended clear; murky vapors were washed away.
translations.idiomatic: Bright qi mingled; murky haze was scoured clean.

sentences.zh: 政才勤倦，妖集廷除。

translations.literal: Government talent waxed diligent and weary; demons gathered at the court gate.
translations.idiomatic: Rule turned from zeal to fatigue; omens clustered at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 先民之言，「靡不有初」。

translations.literal: The words of the ancients: “There is no end without a beginning.”
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: “Nothing lacks a beginning.”
